text:
Alex: FYI NebulaFlow just sent their renewal quote. It's a weird hybrid: minimum monthly commit + per-1k-token usage with separate embedding vs. generation tiers. PDF attached. can someone sanity-check impact for our SearchPilot project?
Maya: I can run a quick mapping. what scale are we planning for SearchPilot? seats vs tokens?
Alex: initial rollout estimates ~1.2B embedding tokens/mo and ~50k gen tokens. seats = 25 (engineers + analytics).
Diego: embedding-heavy indeed. ask them for a sample invoice — we need exact SKU line names so our GL mapping doesn't break. last time vendor used opaque line items and billing ingestion failed.
Elaine: Procurement must see security certs (SOC2 + ISO27001) and an exportable invoice CSV. demand monthly invoices with per-SKU unit_price/unit_quantity columns. no consolidated quarterly lumps.
Maya: Also request an invoice API or S3 export. our billing team wants per-customer, per-route metering (not just aggregated tokens).
Alex: sales said invoices will include lines labeled `commit_credit`, `overage_tokens`, and `seat_charge`. they didn't confirm CSV schema.
Diego: negotiation points: 1) roll-forward unused commit credits for 12 months 2) convert unused credits to seat discounts at invoice time 3) 30-day pilot bucket (500M tokens) at 40% off for validation.
Elaine: add: require pro-rata refund on prepaid seats if we terminate within 6 months. require SLA credit language: any sustained latency over 1s P95 -> credits. also insist on net-30 payment terms and invoice dispute window of 60 days.
billing-bot: Vendor scorecard: NebulaFlow -> Product Fit: B+, Security: A, Pricing Flex: B-. Details: https://redwood-internal/vend-score/NebulaFlow
Maya: for the pricing experiment, can we ask for a meter-export (CSV) for the pilot so we can compare their token counts vs our internal counters? if they don't provide, pilot is worthless.
Alex: sales responded: pilot CSV available but credits expire in 45 days and are non-refundable. asking for extension to 90 days and a refund clause if metering mismatch >5%.
Diego: counter-proposal: 1) 90-day expiry 2) if metering mismatch >3% ensure credit refund equal to discrepancy 3) allow partial roll-forward of unused pilot credits to next billing cycle. include an API call `GET /billing/usage?start=...&end=...` in SOW.
Elaine: legal wants to limit liability but will accept a metering reconciliation clause. finance asks that invoices be in USD with clear FX handling if they bill in EUR. ask for monthly USD invoices.
Maya: quick calc snippet I'm sharing for sales: `monthly_est = seats*seat_rate + (emb_tokens/1000)*embed_rate + (gen_tokens/1000)*gen_rate`
- provide example rates for Tier1 (<1B), Tier2 (1B-5B), Tier3 (>5B).
Alex: good. let's also ask for an overage cap: no more than +25% over committed monthly spend without explicit sign-off.
Diego: pinging sales at 1849123499 requesting: sample invoice CSV, 12-month cost projection at 1.2B tokens/mo, pilot CSV export, SOW snippet with billing API. will escalate to AE if no reply by EOD.
Elaine: once we have their sample invoice + pilot terms, I'll assemble the procurement approval packet (finance + legal checklist). Maya, can you draft a short risk summary (3 bullet points)?
Maya: on it.
Alex: thanks. if they stonewall on CSV/API access, this is a no-go for us. prefer vendors who let us reconcile usage programmatically. :no_entry_sign:
